clue.text: Threaten close friend hiding papers

indicators.note: the close friend conceals the papers within itself, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an intimate is a very close friend
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone threatens to expose a close friend who has been hiding documents.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate someone is to frighten them with menace, which is what threatening does.

clue.text: Bar opponent reportedly getting data

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a bar is an inn, a place to drink; an opponent is a foe

explanation.surface: A pub's rival is rumoured to be gathering intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is the informal short form of information, which is what data supplies.

clue.text: Contaminated meat ain't edible? Just slice away outside bits!

indicators.note: cutting off the outer letters of the phrase leaves a run of letters lying inside it

explanation.surface: A cook warns that spoiled meat is unfit to eat, so trim off the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just slice away outside bits!' tells you to drop MEA from the front and IBLE from the end, leaving the letters hidden in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tainted food has been spoiled or polluted, which is what contaminated means.

clue.text: Ham can imitate cast in summer

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters are thrown or moulded into a new shape

explanation.surface: An overacting actor gets a part to play in a summer production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but one who sums, a classic crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer is someone who adds figures up, and a mathematician works with numbers.

clue.text: Journalist brought up advances for banks

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a senior journalist
to advance an idea is to posit it, put it forward

explanation.surface: A reporter, raised in the trade, gets loans from the banks.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank money is to deposit it; both verbs mean putting funds in an account.

clue.text: Thrive, strangely, having lost five of them

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the word appear in an odd order
having lost says a letter is dropped from the rearranged word

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Some people thrive in odd ways even after losing five of their number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' scrambles THRIVE; 'having lost' then removes the V.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to those people, the same as 'of them'.

clue.text: Counterfoil that's difficult to remove? Not half

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, here the front four of its eight letters

parts.note: a stubborn stain is one that is difficult to remove

explanation.surface: A ticket counterfoil that will not come away, or only half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the British exclamation of emphatic agreement; here it means keep only half.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the part of a ticket or cheque kept as a record, the counterfoil.

clue.text: Credit cancelled for carpet

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick
a cancelled event is off

explanation.surface: A credit purchase on a carpet has been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is the verb, to reprimand, not the floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to scold them, an informal sense matching to reprimand.

clue.text: Relax, then film dance and game

parts.note: to bask is to lie relaxing in warmth
ET is the Spielberg film
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A plan for an evening: unwind, watch a movie, go dancing, play a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Basketball is a team sport, an instance of a game.

clue.text: Rush to capture northern pirate

indicators.note: capturing means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: to flit is to move quickly, to dart

explanation.surface: A dash to seize a pirate in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Flint is the pirate whose treasure is hunted in Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Flint is a famous fictional buccaneer in Stevenson's novel.

clue.text: Police circlingman about in court's grounds

indicators.note: the run-together word reads as policeman circling, the constable going round the next piece

parts.note: PC is a police constable
re means about, concerning
CT is short for court, made plural as CTS

explanation.surface: Officers surround a man near the court buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: The published clue runs 'circling' and 'man' together; it reads best as 'Policeman circling', the constable going round 'about'. 'court's grounds' tempts as the definition, but 'court's' supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Precincts are the enclosed area around a building such as a cathedral, its grounds.

clue.text: Trainees timed changing tyres

indicators.note: changing says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Apprentice mechanics are timed while swapping tyres in a pit stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainees' looks like the definition; it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, intermediates are tyres for damp tracks, between slicks and full wets.

clue.text: Cherish floating voter that was collected by 9?

parts.note: to treasure is to cherish

indicators.note: a floating voter is undecided, and floating signals letters drifting into a new order

explanation.surface: A party hopes to cherish the undecided voter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to 9 across, the pirate Flint, whose hoard is sought in Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate's buried hoard of riches is the sort of valuables found as treasure trove.

clue.text: Change of heart?

parts.note: not a shift of opinion but a surgical swap of the organ for a donor one

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders their opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart operation replacing the organ with a donor's is literally a change of heart.

clue.text: Changes to plan visibly embarrassed crowds

parts.note: an embarrassed person who blushes goes red
rafts means large numbers, as in rafts of people

explanation.surface: Plans are altered when a blushing official faces crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft is to rewrite a document, making changes to the plan.

clue.text: Rep condemned great post-war building

indicators.note: something condemned is broken down, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means great

explanation.surface: A representative denounces a fine house put up after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: PREFABs were factory-built houses put up in Britain after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated house was a typical quick-build home erected after the war.

clue.text: Change disrupted her plans

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A sudden change ruined her plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrapnel is British slang for small change, loose coins in the pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang loose coins are called shrapnel, so it means small change.

clue.text: No d-drink? Drink!

parts.note: the stammer on the first letter shows the drink, gin, said with a stutter, g-gin

explanation.surface: A tipsy refusal of a drink, then an insistence on another.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'd-drink' imitates a stammer, so the drink GIN is also stammered as G-GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is a small measure of spirits, a quarter of a pint.

clue.text: Delight when officer enters valley

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: glee is delight
NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: There is joy when an officer arrives in the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Glencoe is a valley in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Glencoe is a glen in the Highlands of Scotland, a named valley.

clue.text: Happy church always not quite crowded

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: a crowded room is full

explanation.surface: A congregation is pleased its church is nearly always packed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerful means in good spirits, synonymous with happy.

clue.text: Blast food for supporters?

indicators.note: food for supporters puts the food after the supporters, as in a menu meant for them

parts.note: fans are supporters; fan stands for them as in fan club
fare means food

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the food served to football fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'food for supporters' reads as fan fare: fare for the fans.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a loud flourish of trumpets, a blast of brass.

clue.text: Hurry in rain, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an example of water falling from the sky, like snow or hail

explanation.surface: Someone rushes along in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rash haste and moisture falling from clouds, rain being one kind.

clue.text: Long story in Independent upset Irish parliament

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about an independent member upsetting Irish lawmakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War is a famously long narrative.

clue.text: Overcome famous footballer

definitions.meaning: to defeat or get the better of
George, the Northern Irish Manchester United winger

explanation.surface: A celebrated footballer is beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone is to defeat them; George is the celebrated winger of that surname.

clue.text: A boy harbours criminal since uprising

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering something inside

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A lad has been sheltering a crook since the revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' gives CENSI and 'harbours' tucks it into the boy; 'uprising' means rising up, not a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascension is an act of rising up, literally an uprising.

clue.text: Abuse when one pulls out in traffic

indicators.note: pulling out means the piece withdraws and is removed

parts.note: a tirade is a long angry outburst of abuse
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Road rage erupts when a car pulls out into traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' means commerce or dealing, not vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as a noun can mean commerce, dealing in goods, the same as trade.

clue.text: Hiker tired somewhat over long journey

indicators.note: over says the letters are turned back to front
somewhat means only part of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: A walker is rather weary after a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' picks KERT from 'Hiker tired', and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is an arduous long walk or trip.

clue.text: Moving anecdotes about beginning to love one's young

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
moving letters around rearranges them
the beginning of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Touching stories about a parent's love for their young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges ANECDOTES into ADO...ESCENT, which goes 'about' L, the first letter of love; 'one's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescent describes someone in their teens, still young and not yet adult.
